short: Three centuries of Muslim rule over most of the Indian subcontinent.
full:
Babur, a Timurid prince pushed out of Central Asia, beat the far larger army of the Delhi Sultan at Panipat in 1526 using field artillery and mobile horse archers. His grandson Akbar built the durable structure: the mansabdari service, ranked and open to Hindus and Muslims alike, a cash revenue settlement assessed on measured and classified land, and the abolition of the jizya tax on non-Muslims. Under Shah Jahan the empire produced the Taj Mahal and, by some estimates, roughly a quarter of world manufacturing output.

Aurangzeb extended it furthest south and spent his last twenty-five years fighting the Marathas in the Deccan at ruinous cost. After his death in 1707 the provinces became independent in all but name, Nadir Shah sacked Delhi in 1739, and the East India Company took the revenues of Bengal after Plassey. The emperor was a Company pensioner long before the end: Bahadur Shah II was deposed and exiled to Rangoon in 1857 for his nominal part in the rebellion.
